at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

at-0005.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
at-0005.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`). Apply it to both the argument and `sub.started_at`.

at-0006.title: Compute periods via floor division
at-0006.content: Compute subscription period boundaries the same way as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`: `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)`, `n = (at - start) // length`, then `start + n * length`. Reuse this pattern instead of looping or using date arithmetic.

at-0007.title: Money-moving functions take keyword-only idempotency_key
at-0007.content: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Check it first, before state validation, by scanning `audit.events(...)` for a matching entry and returning the original record; include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry written.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
